annotations.title: See or change a workbook's settings

description: Renames, retitles or moves a workbook to another folder (`folder`), sets who its members are, and changes how its runs work (mode, model, harness, time limit). To email or share it, or save its sources, use share_workbook. A workbook's settings, and changes to them: its `name`; its `title` — what it is shown by, where that is shorter than its name; its `mode` — `harnessroom`, `latticeroom`, `graphroom`, `flashroom` or `askroom` (a harnessroom researches and writes; a latticeroom is handed a draft and marks each claim with its sources, and each reference with whether the work exists, leaving the words as written; a graphroom performs the procedure drawn for it in the app; a flashroom plans an edit to its spreadsheet and makes it on `yes`; an askroom answers questions of the document and never changes it); for a harnessroom, the `model` its runs think with (one of the `nodes` this answers with), the `harness` that drives it, the time a run gets — `time_limit_minutes`, or `time_limit_seconds` for a run someone waits on — and its `economy`; the `members` it belongs to; and the `storage` its runs file sources into. Send only what should change — the rest stays. With nothing to change it only reads. Changes apply from the next run.

economy.description: How a harnessroom run keeps its transcript small: compaction (the default), steering, delegation, or unbounded.

folder.description: Move it to this folder; empty for the top level.

harness.description: The coding harness that drives a harnessroom run.

members.description: Every member's email, the whole list: who the workbook is shared with and who its email goes to.

mode.description: What this workbook's runs are, from now on. `harnessroom` (a new workbook's default): the instruction is a request, and a harness researches and writes the document. `latticeroom`: the instruction is a draft someone already wrote, whole — markdown, its links kept — which comes back exactly as written, with the run's inference beside it (read_workbook's `inference`: each claim cited, self-reported, secondary only, contradicted or with no source, and its sources); each entry under its References or Bibliography heading is looked up in Crossref and on the web and marked found, found with other authors or year, or not found, and a sentence citing it — [3], (Smith et al., 2020) — is read against the work found; attach data files (.json, .csv, .tsv) to settle the draft's own figures. `graphroom`: runs perform the procedure drawn for the workbook in the app, and refuse until one is drawn. `flashroom`, for a workbook made from a spreadsheet or a Word document: the instruction is an edit to its sheet, or to the document's table it is about, planned in seconds and kept in `messages` — each cell's before and after, the rows added and removed — and nothing is written until the next instruction is `yes`, which makes it as a new version. `askroom`: the workbook is asked and never changed — every instruction is a question of the document as it stands, answered in seconds and kept in `messages`; no run writes a version. A mirror's read-only copy is always an askroom. Omit to keep the workbook's current mode.

model.description: The model a harnessroom's runs think with: a `node` from this tool's answer.

name.description: A new name for the workbook.

sealed.description: true seals a harnessroom's runs: each sees the web, the programs and its own /tmp, and nothing an earlier run left — no drive, no attachments, no other workbook. For a measurement that must not be handed earlier research.

storage.description: Where runs file the sources they save: a connected drive, or auto (the first connected).

time_limit_minutes.description: How long a harnessroom run may take before it is stopped.

time_limit_seconds.description: The same in seconds, for a run a person waits on: stopped there, it delivers the draft it has written. Give this or time_limit_minutes, not both.

title.description: What it is shown by, over its name. Need not be unique. An empty string clears it.

name: configure_workbook
title: See or change a workbook's settings
